named_public_import_and_scope: Sang-Jun Park, k-Positivity and high-dimensional bound entanglement under symplectic group symmetry, arXiv:2602.09860v1, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.09860v1, especially Theorems 1.2 and 3.4. The map family and its cone classification are public prior art; the attribution and Choi convention are reconstructed explicitly below. The four-vertex criterion and compression decomposition are independently argued here, not treated as adopted from f216. This is one self-contained post-contact packet; no Johnston–Lovitz article, held material, selected-parameter episode, or fixed-KG variant is used.
main_theorem: Let d>=4 be even, k>=2 even with 2k<=d, and J be any skew-symmetric unitary. Every k-positive map Phi(Z)=a Tr(Z)I_d+bZ+c J Z^T J^*, with real a,b,c, has decomposable Choi compression to every input or output subspace of dimension at most 2k. Equivalently, for every PPT state rho on C^d tensor C^d and local filters A,B, the Choi expectation after filtering is nonnegative whenever rank(A)<=2k OR rank(B)<=2k. This remains true for finite sums of arbitrary local completely-positive images of such witnesses and of decomposable witnesses. In particular, for k=2 no member or such CP-generated sum can supply a rank<=4 negative filter on ANY PPT source. These maps include genuinely indecomposable examples when d>2k. This is an obstruction for the specified map cone, not a global 4x4 PPT/SN3 conclusion.
normalization_and_attribution: For nonzero positive Phi, s=ad+b+c>0 because Phi(I)=sI and a positive map vanishing at I is zero. Divide by s and put t=a/s, p=b/s, q=c/s, so dt+p+q=1 and Phi_(p,q)(Z)=t Tr(Z)I+pZ+qJZ^T J^*. Its unnormalized Choi matrix is C=t I+p[Omega]+q(I tensor J)F(I tensor J^*), where Omega=sum_i|ii>. Conjugating by the local unitary I tensor J^* gives C_hat=t I+p[j]+qF with j=(I tensor J^*)Omega=vec(conjugate(J)); j is the vectorization of a skew-unitary matrix, Fj=-j, and ||j||^2=d. The Park BH_k point p=-1/(kd-k-1), q=-k/(kd-k-1) has t=k/(kd-k-1); therefore C_hat=(kI-kF-[j])/(kd-k-1), exactly the form used below. A local unitary does not change decomposability or the ranks of local filters.
four_necessary_tests: Write F-expectation f and h=|<j|x>|^2 for a unit vector x of Schmidt rank <=k. The four tests are: (i) |e_1,e_1> has (f,h)=(1,0); (ii) (|e_1,e_2>-|e_2,e_1>)/sqrt(2), using two vectors in a symplectic isotropic subspace, has (-1,0); (iii) the normalized sum over k/2 full symplectic pairs (|e_i,f_i>-|f_i,e_i>)/sqrt(k) has (-1,k); (iv) the normalized sum over k distinct symplectic pairs |e_i,f_i>/sqrt(k) has (0,k). These exist exactly under k even and 2k<=d. Positivity on them forces u=t+q>=0, v=t-q>=0, w=t-q+kp>=0, x=t+kp>=0.
independent_four_vertex_cone: The normalized intersection of these four halfplanes is a bounded quadrilateral with vertices A=(p,q)=(1,0), B=(0,1/(d+1)), C=(-1/(kd-1),0), D=(-1/(kd-k-1),-k/(kd-k-1)). Consecutive equalities u=v, v=w, w=x, x=u give A,B,C,D. The other two pairwise intersections violate respectively x>=0 or w>=0, and boundedness follows from t>=|q| and x>=0 together with dt+p+q=1. At A the map is CP. At B its rotated Choi matrix is (I+F)/(d+1)>=0. At C the map is (k Tr(Z)I-Z)/(kd-1), both k-positive by |<Omega|y>|^2<=k||y||^2 for rank<=k y, and completely copositive because its Choi partial transpose is (kI-F)/(kd-1)>=0. At D the map is BH_k; if Y has rank<=k, S=(Y-Y^T)/2 has rank<=2k and |Tr(J^*S)|^2<=2k||S||_F^2, so kI-kF-[j] is k-block positive. Thus all four vertices are k-positive, and the four necessary tests are also sufficient. Every normalized map in this family is their convex combination; no reliance on the public cone formula is needed for this written proof.
bh_compression_canonical_form: For any 2k-dimensional isometry U, write E=ran(U), choose a complement U_perp, and let K=U^*J conjugate(U), N=U^*J conjugate(U_perp). The standard complex skew-unitary-congruence normal form gives K=direct_sum_i lambda_i[[0,1],[-1,0]], 0<=lambda_i<=1. Since KK^*+NN^*=I, put s_i=sqrt(1-lambda_i^2); the nonzero row pairs of N are mutually orthogonal and can be aligned with distinct pairs p_i,q_i of output-complement coordinates. After these local basis choices, j_U=(U^* tensor I)j=sum_i lambda_i a_i+sum_(s_i>0)s_i c_i, with a_i=|2i-1,2i>-|2i,2i-1> and c_i=|2i-1,p_i>-|2i,q_i>. These mutually orthogonal vectors have squared norm 2, and sum lambda_i^2+sum s_i^2=k. The compressed Choi matrix is C_U=k I-kF_E-[j_U], where F_E is swap on the input/output E block and zero on the output complement. The skew-unitary congruence theorem is a named standard linear-algebra import.
bh_compression_psd_plus_copositive: For each defective pair set h_i=|2i-1,q_i>+|2i,p_i>. Let u_alpha list the a_i and defective c_i and w_alpha their respective lambda_i and s_i. Let A_other contain unnormalized antisymmetric |p,q>-|q,p> in the input/E block except the k paired a_i, and B_other the standard |p,o> with output o outside E except the 2x2 input/output block of each defective pair. Then C_U=P+k sum_(s_i>0)[h_i]^Gamma_in, where P=sum_(alpha<beta)[w_alpha u_beta-w_beta u_alpha]+k sum_(v in A_other)[v]+k sum_(v in B_other)[v] is explicitly PSD. Indeed kI-kF_E equals 2k on the antisymmetric E sector, 0 on the symmetric E sector and k outside E. Each [h_i]^Gamma has eigenvalue -1 on c_i, +1 on its symmetric companion and on the two cross basis vectors in that defective 2x2 block. The remaining span of the normalized u_alpha has diagonal 2k, while [j_U] is 2ww^T with ||w||^2=k; the first PSD sum equals 2(kI-ww^T). All other PSD terms are exactly as displayed. Smaller input ranks follow by isometric extension and completely-positive precomposition. Since C_hat=tI+p[j]+qF is swap invariant, the same conclusion holds for output compression.
all_sources_and_cp_closure: A Hermitian witness C has no rank<=r input-filter negative pairing on any PPT source iff every r-dimensional input compression is decomposable: the forward direction uses the duality between the PPT cone and P+Q^Gamma with P,Q>=0, and the reverse uses preservation of PPT under local CP filtering. The decomposable cone is closed because the traces of PSD P,Q are nonnegative and sum to the trace of P+Q^Gamma. Intersections of these compression cones are closed and convex. Local CP images preserve the property: after a rank<=r filter, each Kraus summand has an effective filter of rank <=r, and decomposable compressed witnesses remain decomposable under the other local CP map. Sums and added decomposable witnesses preserve it. The generated maps remain k-positive when all added terms are themselves k-positive; the no-PPT-pairing statement does not require that extra hypothesis.
nontriviality_and_scope: This obstruction is not just global decomposability. For d>2k, R=I+F+[j] is PSD because I+F>=0, and R^Gamma=I+[Omega]+(I tensor conjugate(J))F(I tensor conjugate(J)^*) is PSD because the twisted swap is a Hermitian involution. Moreover Tr[(kI-kF-[j])R]=d(2k-d)<0, so BH_k is indecomposable. In fact, mixing the normalized BH_k point with the identity map by weight lambda in 0<=lambda<(d-2k)/(d-2k+d(kd-k-1)) retains negative pairing with R, while every rank<=2k compression is decomposable; for d=6,k=2 the interval is 0<=lambda<1/28. The original 4x4 PPT/SN3 target remains OPEN and no general nonexistence is claimed.
